Supply tax

Before the tax, demand and supply meet at Q0=5Q_0=5Q0​=5 and P0=7P_0=7P0​=7

A four-dollar tax creates a wedge between the price consumers pay and the price producers receive: Pc=Pp+4P_c=P_p+4Pc​=Pp​+4

On a graph whose vertical axis is the consumer price, demand stays put because willingness to pay has not changed; buyer-facing supply rises by four dollars

Their new intersection has consumers paying Pc=9P_c=9Pc​=9 while producers receive Pp=5P_p=5Pp​=5

and trade contracts from Q0=5Q_0=5Q0​=5 units to Qt=3Q_t=3Qt​=3

Before the tax, consumer and producer surplus fill the gains-from-trade region, 25/225/225/2 each; afterward, the surviving portions are only 9/29/29/2 each

One part of the missing private surplus becomes government revenue: the four-dollar wedge across three traded units is 4⋅3=124\cdot3=124⋅3=12

The remaining triangle is not transferred to anyone: the prevented trades between Qt=3Q_t=3Qt​=3 and Q0=5Q_0=5Q0​=5 leave 444 of deadweight loss
